function.name: calculate_Bond_Price
function.description: Calculate the bond price based on its face value, coupon rate, required rate of return, and the number of years until maturity. The calculation assumes annual coupon payments. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

Face_Value.description: The nominal value or par value of the bond in dollars. This is a float type value.

Coupon_rate.description: The annual coupon rate of the bond expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

Required_return.description: The annual required rate of return for the bond investment expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

maturity_years.description: The number of whole years until the bond's maturity.

message.content:
I don’t have real‑time market data, so I can’t give you the exact price of gold for today.  Gold is quoted in U.S. dollars per troy ounce and the price changes every few seconds during trading hours.

**How to find the current price**

| Source | What you’ll see | How to access |
|--------|-----------------|---------------|
| **Kitco** | Live gold price, charts, news | <https://www.kitco.com> |
| **Bloomberg** | Real‑time commodity prices, analysis | <https://www.bloomberg.com/markets/commodities> |
| **Reuters** | Live gold price, market commentary | <https://www.reuters.com/markets/commodities> |
| **Investing.com** | Live gold price, technical charts | <https://www.investing.com/commodities/gold> |
| **Yahoo Finance** | Current gold price, historical data | <https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/GC=F> |

If you’re looking for the most up‑to‑date figure, check one of those sites or your brokerage’s market data feed.  The price will be shown in U.S. dollars per ounce (e.g., “$1,950.25/oz”).
message.reasoning: User asks: "What is the gold price today in USA?" We need to provide current gold price. We don't have real-time data. We can say we don't have real-time data, but can provide approximate or typical price. We can also mention that gold price is typically quoted in US dollars per ounce. We can provide a link or suggestion to check reliable sources like Bloomberg, Kitco, etc. We should not fabricate. So answer: "I don't have real-time data, but as of last known data, gold was around $X per ounce." But we don't know X. We could say "As of the last market close, gold was trading at approximately $1,950 per ounce." But that might be inaccurate. Better to say "I don't have real-time data, but you can check the latest price on websites like Kitco, Bloomberg, etc." Also mention that gold price fluctuates. So answer accordingly.
